name: U.S. Department of the Treasury

summary.text: The U.S. Department of the Treasury was established by Act of Congress on September 2, 1789, with Alexander Hamilton as its first Secretary. Its website states that its mission is to maintain a strong economy and create economic and job opportunities by promoting the conditions that enable economic growth and stability at home and abroad, and that it also strengthens national security by combating threats and protecting the integrity of the financial system; its functions include producing coin and currency, collecting revenue, borrowing to fund the government and implementing economic sanctions. On this site it appears through the 1974 U.S.-Saudi Joint Commission and the Treasury securities 'add-on' facility, the 1995 Mexico support package from the Exchange Stabilization Fund, the 2008 Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac conservatorships, and its rulemaking under the 2025 GENIUS Act.

facts.claim: The Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation established with Saudi Arabia on June 8, 1974 was co-chaired by the U.S. Treasury Secretary and the Saudi Minister of Finance and National Economy, and its U.S. technical assistance was funded almost entirely from the Saudi Arabian Trust Account held at the U.S. Treasury, according to GAO.
facts.quote: U.S. technical assistance is funded almost entirely from the Saudi Arabian Trust Account in the U.S. Treasury.

sources.title: The U.S.-Saudi Arabian Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation (ID-79-7)

facts.claim: GAO reported in 1979 that the Treasury's noncompetitive 'add-on' facility for purchasing Treasury securities outside the competitive auctions was first offered to Saudi Arabia and was by then available to all governments and central banks.
facts.quote: The noncompetitive 'add-on' purchase facility for Treasury securities was first offered to Saudi Arabia, and it is now available to all governments and central banks.

facts.claim: On January 31, 1995 the United States announced it would provide Mexico up to $20 billion through the Exchange Stabilization Fund and the Federal Reserve swap network, as part of a $48.8 billion multilateral package, combining short-term swaps, medium-term swaps of up to five years and securities guarantees of up to ten years. By December 22, 1995, $13.5 billion had been disbursed and no securities guarantees had been extended.
facts.quote: The package was a combination of short-term swaps with renewals allowed, medium-term swaps of up to 5 years, and securities guarantees with terms of up to 10 years.

sources.title: Mexico's Financial Crisis: Origins, Awareness, Assistance, and Initial Efforts to Recover (GGD-96-56)
Exchange Stabilization Fund: Finances and Operations

facts.claim: Treasury's own account of the Exchange Stabilization Fund says that when the ESF provided financial support for Mexico in 1995 it was through a medium-term credit, and that the ESF has historically been used to buy and sell foreign currencies, extend short-term swaps to foreign countries and guarantee obligations of foreign governments.
facts.quote: when the ESF provided financial support for Mexico in 1995, it was through a medium-term credit

sources.title: Exchange Stabilization Fund: Finances and Operations

facts.claim: On September 7, 2008 Treasury announced that the Federal Housing Finance Agency had placed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship and that Treasury had entered Preferred Stock Purchase Agreements committing it to keep each company's net worth positive in exchange for senior preferred shares and warrants.
facts.quote: Statement by Secretary Henry M. Paulson, Jr. on Treasury and Federal Housing Finance Agency Action to Protect Financial Markets and Taxpayers

sources.title: Statement by Secretary Henry M. Paulson, Jr. on Treasury and Federal Housing Finance Agency Action to Protect Financial Markets and Taxpayers

facts.claim: Following enactment of the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27) on July 18, 2025, Treasury issued a request for comment that it said fulfilled its obligation under section 9(a) of the Act, and on September 18, 2025 an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on implementation; in 2026 it proposed rules on state-level regulatory regimes, on illicit-finance requirements (jointly through FinCEN and OFAC) and on the issuance of payment stablecoins.
facts.quote: Today's request for comment fulfills Treasury's obligation pursuant to section 9(a) of the GENIUS Act, which creates a comprehensive regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers in the United States.

facts.claim: On November 21, 2023 Treasury announced settlements with Binance that it described as the largest in its history: a $3.4 billion FinCEN civil money penalty and an OFAC settlement of about $968 million, alongside the Justice Department's criminal resolution.
facts.quote: U.S. Treasury Announces Largest Settlements in History with World's Largest Virtual Currency Exchange Binance for Violations of U.S. Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Laws
